chunks: Whoever performs the Maghrib prayer, then does ta'qib and does not speak until he prays two rak'ahs, they are written for him in 'Illiyyin. If he prays four, an accepted hajj is written for him.

key_terms.عَقَّبَ: performed ta'qib, the post-prayer devotional acts
key_terms.عِلِّيِّينَ: the highest exalted register or rank

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for performing ta'qib and extra rak'ahs after Maghrib without speaking?
ai.summary: This hadith encourages maintaining devotion after Maghrib through ta'qib and additional prayer before speaking. It describes a great reward for two rak'ahs and an even greater reward for four, showing the spiritual merit of post-prayer worship.
